title: CPOM Antarctic cumulative surface elevation change since March 1995, multi-mission radar altimetry
product_version: CPOM multi-mission radar altimetry surface elevation change, Antarctica, 5 km, product version 1.0 (fv1)
reference: Shepherd, A. et al. (2019): Trends in Antarctic Ice Sheet elevation and mass. Geophysical Research Letters 46, 8174-8183. doi:10.1029/2019GL082182
license: CC BY 4.0 (the CPOM files' licence); cite the sources listed under `sources`

dataset.citation: Centre for Polar Observation and Modelling (2026): Antarctic Ice Sheet surface elevation change at 5 km from multi-mission radar altimetry (ERS-2, Envisat, CryoSat-2), product version 1.0. CPOM Land Ice Portal.
dataset.creators: A. Muir, T. Slater, J. Maddalena, B. Palmer (CPOM)

paper.citation: Shepherd, A. et al. (2019): Trends in Antarctic Ice Sheet elevation and mass. Geophysical Research Letters 46, 8174-8183.

sources.missions: ERS-2 and Envisat (ESA FDR4ALT Land Ice Thematic Data Product v1) and CryoSat-2 (ESA Cryo-TEMPO Land Ice, Baseline D)

resampling.method: area-weighted mean of the 5 km CPOM cells overlapping each explorer cell
resampling.drawn_on: explorer ice cells (BedMachine Antarctica v4 grounded ice, floating ice and Lake Vostok)
resampling.reason: CPOM's cells are on a 5 km EPSG:3031 grid of their own; overlay and terrain cells must correspond one to one
resampling.rows: CPOM rows run south to north and are flipped

domain.order: row-major order of the non-zero cells of domain_mask

frames.layout: frame-major: surface_change[frame * cell_count + cell]; final_uncertainty and the domain have one value per cell
frames.note: each frame is one 140-day epoch, placed at its centre, with CPOM's published change relative to its 1995 reference level; the first epoch departs from that level and is not subtracted

series.note: CPOM's cumulative mass change of the grounded ice sheet, of the IMBIE regions and of the 18 IMBIE drainage basins (numbered as in CPOM's basin_id, which cites Rignot et al. 2016), 1-sigma, from the portal's basin time series; sea-level equivalent at 362.5 Gt per mm

pole_hole.note: south of 81.5 S the change is extrapolated until CryoSat-2 data arrive (the first epoch whose increments vary across 82-87 S); south of 88 S it is extrapolated throughout

visualization.fade_note: a frame's change is faded where it is smaller than twice final_uncertainty

validation.note: volume change relative to CPOM's 1995 reference level at the last epoch (grid area, no map-scale correction), over every CPOM cell and over the packed domain cells. The net is a small residual of thickening and thinning that nearly cancel, so it moves with the margins; averaging to 10 km also cancels opposite-signed changes within a cell, which lowers both gross volumes
validation.basin_sum_note: largest gap over the epochs between each region's series and the sum of its basins' series

fields.name: final_uncertainty
fields.note: 1-sigma uncertainty of the cumulative change at the last epoch, one value per domain cell; CPOM's per-epoch uncertainty is zero for most cells before 2002, so it is not stored per frame

flags.1: explorer ice cell with a CPOM value in the last epoch
